_doc: Revert-verify mutants for ticket 9a829c1b (RFC-017 tail, branch batch7b/vocabulary-namespace-forprefix). Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute). The production diff is ONE expression: RDFVocabularyMapper.generateMappedTriple used to resolve the namespace of a `prefix__LocalName` STRING value by enumerating three prefixes in a regex (`/^(ems|exo|exocmd)__(.+)$/` plus a ternary over Namespace.EMS/EXOCMD/EXO); it now calls Namespace.fromPropertyKey → forPrefix, the same data-driven resolver NoteToRDFConverter already applies upstream (isClassReference :1960 / expandClassValue :1986). Guards are enumerated INSIDE that expression per integration-test-revert-verify §A8: the resolver choice itself (M1), the not-a-prefix fallback (M2), and the local-name extraction (M3). ⛤ REACHABILITY, measured not assumed: the single production consumer (NoteToRDFConverter.ts:511) gates the call on `objectNode instanceof IRI`, and a `prefix__LocalName` value — wikilink `[[pmbok__RiskItem]]` or flat `person__Person` alike — is already resolved to a symbolic IRI upstream, so this string branch takes 0 of 2 calls on the production path (instrumented probe against the built dist, PR body). The branch IS exercised by this suite and by external callers of the exported class, which is why every axis drives the public method directly and none of them claims a vault-conversion effect. ⛔ N4 is a CONTROL, not an axis: it pins the `value instanceof IRI` passthrough — the production path — and stays GREEN under every mutant. That is the point: it shows the three mutants perturb only the string branch and leave the path the vault actually uses untouched. A mutant reddening N4 would mean the diff had escaped its own branch. ⛤ ONE conceivable mutation carries no mutant, by arithmetic rather than omission: dropping the leading `value instanceof IRI` check is NOT part of this diff (that branch is pre-existing and unchanged), so mutating it would measure someone else's guard — §A8 enumerates the guards of THIS expression. Expectations were derived axis-by-axis (what does each one assert) and written down BEFORE the run, per §A44.

M1_three_prefix_enumeration_restored._note: The pre-fix code verbatim (the whole point of the ticket). Type-preserving: objectIRI stays IRI on both branches. Must redden N1 ONLY — `pmbok__RiskItem` falls through to `new IRI(value)`, which throws "Invalid IRI format"; the three enumerated prefixes (N2) and the not-a-prefix fallback (N3) behave identically under both forms, which is exactly the byte-identity claim this PR makes.

M2_not_a_prefix_fallback_dropped._note: Removes the branch that keeps a non-`prefix__LocalName` value (a full IRI, a plain label) on the raw-IRI path. Type-preserving via the non-null assertion — the mutant compiles and throws at runtime on the very input N3 supplies. N1/N2 are unaffected: their values DO parse, so `parsed` is non-null and the fallback is never taken.

M3_local_name_ignored._note: Keeps the data-driven namespace but mints the term from the WHOLE value, so `pmbok__RiskItem` becomes `…/pmbok#pmbok__RiskItem`. Reddens both the new-prefix axis and the byte-identity control — the latter is what proves N2 is not decorative: it pins the exact IRI string, not merely 'some IRI'.
